exam: Diagrams 2 - class diagram, decision tree, storyboard (real questions)

parts.prompt:
**A school is designing a class diagram for its online library system.**

Each **Book** has:
- A title
- An ISBN number
- A category (e.g. "Fiction", "Non-Fiction", "Reference")
- Assume there is only one of each book in this library

Each **Student**:
- Has a name and student ID
- Can borrow multiple books

Each **Loan**:
- A student can loan books
- A loan records the due date and whether the book has been returned
- Can have many books in one loan

**Draw a UML class diagram in markdown format that models this system.**
Include class names, attributes, and relationships.
parts.sample_answer:
**UML Class Diagram**

```plaintext
+---------------------------+
|         Student           |
+---------------------------+
| - name: String            |
| - studentID: String       |
+---------------------------+
           | 1
           |
           | *
+---------------------------+
|           Loan            |
+---------------------------+
| - loanID: String          |
| - dueDate: Date           |
| - returned: Boolean       |
+---------------------------+
           | 1
           |
           | *
+---------------------------+
|           Book            |
+---------------------------+
| - title: String           |
| - isbn: String            |
| - category: String        |
+---------------------------+
```

**Relationships:**
- A **Student** can have **many Loans** → `Student 1 → * Loan`
- Each **Loan** is linked to **one Student**
- A **Loan** can include **many Books** → `Loan 1 → * Book`
- Each **Book** belongs to **one Loan**

questions.title: Decision Tree (Draw/MC, TKS 2025)
questions.stimulus:
A hospital uses a smart monitoring system to assess patients' vital signs and decide whether to alert medical staff or take automated action.

1\. If the patient is currently being monitored in **real time**:

-   The system checks the **heart rate** (HR).
    
    -   If the heart rate is **abnormally high or low**, it checks the **patient's alert status**.
        
        -   If the patient is **conscious**, it **sends an alert to the attending nurse**.
            
        -   If the patient is **unconscious**, it **triggers a code blue response**.
            
    -   If the heart rate is **within the normal range**, it checks the **oxygen level** (SpO2).
        
        -   If oxygen is **below 95%**, it **administers oxygen automatically** and **logs the event**.
            
        -   If oxygen is **normal**, it does **nothing**.
            

2\. If the patient is **not** currently under **real-time monitoring**:

-   The system checks whether the **patient has a chronic condition**.
    
    -   If **yes**, it checks whether **a check-in is overdue**.
        
        -   If **yes**, it **sends a remote check-in prompt**.
            
        -   If **no**, it **schedules the next routine check**.
            
    -   If **no chronic condition**, it checks whether the patient has had **any new symptoms reported** in the past 24 hours.
        
        -   If **yes**, it **requests a nurse** to examine patient.
            
        -   If **no**, it does **nothing**.

parts.prompt: Construct a decision tree to represent the logical process used by the smart patient monitoring system.

marking_criteria.criterion: Draws a substantially correct decision tree showing all rules and actions
Draws a partially correct decision tree showing all rules and actions
Draws a decision tree showing understanding of some rules and actions
Identifies some features of a decision tree

questions.title: Designing, Modelling, and Planning the Development and Deployment of a Visitor Check-In System (Question 26, ITE 2015)
questions.stimulus:
Green Mountain School has engaged Good Software, a software development company, to  build a new electronic visitor check-in system for the school. Good Software consists of a  small team of five developers who work on custom software projects for small to medium  businesses. It is a distributed team with the developers working from home in locations all  around the country. 

Currently when visitors arrive at the school they need to check-in by writing their details  into a visitor log book, and then be issued with a non-personalised visitors badge. 

With this new system, when a visitor arrives at school reception they will type their name  into a tablet computer, along with their email address and the staff member who they are  visiting (this field will autocomplete from the school’s staff database). If they have not  visited the school before they will be prompted to read and agree to the school’s evacuation  and lockdown policies – they only need to agree to the policies once, as the system will  remember if they have visited previously and already registered their agreement (using their  email address which is assumed to be unique to each visitor). The visitor’s details will be  stored in a database on the tablet along with the date and time of their check-in. Finally, a  name label for the visit will be printed on a connected label printer with their name. 

The system needs to be built within one month. Good Software intend to build the software  using a development environment called DatabasePro, a database application available for  the tablet device.

parts.prompt: Draw a storyboard for this system.

marking_criteria.criterion: A comprehensive storyboard showing features of the screens and links between screens.
A comprehensive design of at least two screens, with links between the screens.
A comprehensive design of at least one screen.
An attempt at designing a single screen.
